AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the rails that move money into, out of and across Float: financial ledgering, financial accounts, payment rails (EFT, wires, ACH, cross-border and FX) and card infrastructure. Reporting to the GM, Banking, you'll work across three engineering squads to build and maintain the infrastructure behind our corporate cards, payments, FX and banking products. You'll think about the whole life of a payment — how it starts, how its status is communicated, what happens when it fails or is returned, and how customers and our teams resolve exceptions. You'll work with a designer, eight engineers and a product operations specialist focused on analytics and go-to-market planning.



WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Own the Financial Infrastructure roadmap end to end: sizing, sequencing, delivery, launch and iteration.

 - Make payment health measurable and keep improving it — success rate, processing speed, failure recovery and reconciliation.

 - Evaluate and manage infrastructure partners with our Product Partnerships team, including partner changes and new rail launches.

 - Manage dependencies with banks, networks and processors that move on their own timelines. Escalate risks early, with options attached.

 - Partner closely with Engineering on APIs, data models, ledger interactions, controls and observability.

 - Make trade-off calls across customer experience, speed, reliability, risk, compliance, operational complexity and commercial impact.

 - Coordinate across our card, payments and banking products so infrastructure work supports the whole business.

 - Learn how finance leaders run payroll funding, tax remittance and multi-currency treasury, and work with Design to build accounts, treasury and FX into those workflows.

 - Use AI tools to speed up discovery, analysis, documentation and decision-making.



ABOUT YOU

 - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role.

 - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.



WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 5+ years in product management, with hands-on experience building and maintaining financial services infrastructure at a startup or scale-up.

 - Direct ownership of financial ledgering, money movement or payments products.

 - Experience leading a major infrastructure change — such as moving volume to a new bank partner or replacing a core system — while keeping customers and compliance whole.

 - Strong project management across external partners with their own timelines.

 - Clear, proactive written communication; people know where things stand before they ask.

 - Comfort with engineering concepts such as APIs, data models, ledgers and observability.

   - Experience working directly with sponsor banks, payment processors and payment networks.
   
   - Experience building business banking, treasury management, accounts payable or accounts receivable products.
     
     


THIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF

 - You treat Risk, Compliance or Operations as downstream approvers rather than product partners.

 - You focus on the happy path and leave failures, returns, reconciliation or operational tooling for someone else.

 - You'd rather run one big launch than keep many improvements moving at once.

 - You struggle to connect product decisions to measurable customer and business outcomes.

 - You're resistant to AI-enabled ways of working.




WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN

 - Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits

 - Thrive in a high-trust, high-performance culture where your work truly matters

 


OUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY

We hire for character, curiosity, and learning velocity before credentials. Titles matter less than impact, and every hire is expected to raise the bar for Float as a whole.

 


IN SHORT

At Float, you’ll thrive if you’re bold, curious, and eager to make a real impact. We're building something special—and having a lot of fun along the way. If you’re excited to build, grow, and win together, we’d love to meet you.

 Infrastructure as Code : Rédiger et maintenir le code Pulumi pour automatiser le provisionnement des ressources cloud nécessaires aux applications. Créer des modules réutilisables en .NET ou Python.

 Description

 Infrastructure as Code: Experience with IaC tools such as Pulumi, Terraform, or equivalent.

 Group RRSP.

 Taiga is a Canadian company reinventing the powersports industry through revolutionary electric off-road vehicles.  Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
 The role
 Okta enables universal, secure access to technology for every user and organization. Okta Customer Identity (OCI) is the identity platform behind that promise for the applications our customers build for their own customers: the login, MFA, and account management layer for millions of end users across B2B, B2B2C and B2C products. OCI sits alongside Okta Workforce Identity (OWI) as one of the two halves of the Okta platform.
 We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to grow OCI's footprint inside our existing enterprise base and to incubate the next generation of platform capabilities. This is a builder's role. You'll spend a good chunk of your time in true zero-to-one territory: sizing a raw opportunity, proving it out with a design partner or two, and turning it into a capability that ships and gets adopted. You'll spend the rest of it as the connective tissue across engineering, design, research, and go-to-market, making sure those bets land in the field.
 What you will own
 New Capability Incubation: Own the pipeline of zero-to-one bets on the Okta’s Okta Customer Identity platform, from a rough problem statement through a validated design and a shipped v1. You'll decide what's worth building before anyone asks engineering to build it.
 Platform Growth: Drive the product side of Okta Customer Identity platform expansion into our existing enterprise base. You'll turn a hypothesis about why they haven't adopted the Okta Customer Identity platform into product changes that remove the reason.
 Cross-functional Delivery: Be the person engineering, design, research, and go-to-market call when a new Okta Customer Identity platform capability needs a decision. You'll write the specs, run the reviews, and keep a dozen loosely connected workstreams moving toward the same launch.
 A day in the life
 Your day splits between zero-to-one thinking and shipping discipline. You might start the morning studying churn or expansion data for a segment we don't serve well yet, trying to figure out whether the gap is a feature gap or a positioning gap. An hour later you're on a call with a design partner customer, walking through a rough prototype and taking notes on what confused them.
 By midday you're in execution mode: reviewing a spec with your engineering lead, debating whether a capability needs its own data model or can extend an existing one, and pushing back on scope that's grown past what the opportunity actually justifies. You write plainly. Your specs read like an explanation to a smart colleague, not a wish list.
 In the afternoon you sync with go-to-market and your PMM partner on how a capability in progress should be positioned once it ships, and you flag anything that changes the pitch. You close the day presenting to a customer or prospect, walking them through what's shipped and what's coming on the roadmap. 
 Responsibilities
 Identify, size, and validate new zero-to-one opportunities on the Okta Customer Identity platform, using customer conversations, usage data, and market signals rather than internal opinion alone.
 Define and execute a roadmap that balances new capability bets against platform reliability, security hardening, and performance
 Write clear, detailed specs and requirements that give engineering and design unambiguous direction, especially in areas with no existing playbook.
 Partner with sales, customer success, and product marketing to turn a shipped capability into an adopted one, including understanding why customers who should adopt haven't.
 Track the CIAM market and competitive moves from Auth0, Microsoft, and Ping, and use that context to sharpen where the Okta Customer Identity platform should and shouldn't compete.
 Be the go-to expert for your area of the Okta Customer Identity platform roadmap in front of customers, executives, and cross-functional partners.

 Strong written and verbal communication. You can write a spec an engineer can build from and a one-pager an executive can act on, without changing the substance between the two.
 Strong analytical and decision-making skills. You can build a credible plan from incomplete or conflicting inputs, and explain the assumptions behind it.
 BS in Computer Science, Business, or an equivalent background, with the ability to hold your own in a design review with engineering and architecture.

 Public speaking experience, ideally in front of customers or at industry events.
 MBA or equivalent graduate business degree.
 Top 3 qualities we are hiring for
 Zero-to-one conviction: You've taken a fuzzy opportunity from "should we even do this?" to a shipped, adopted capability, without a playbook telling you how. You know the difference between not validated yet and not going to work, and you don't confuse the two.

You explicitly name your assumptions, move fast, and revise them in public without ego when new information arrives.

ABOUT COHERE AND NORTH

Cohere is revolutionizing enterprise AI with North, an agentic AI platform designed to securely deploy AI agents and automations within organizations' infrastructure. North empowers employees to streamline workflows, automate repetitive tasks, and unlock actionable insights while ensuring data privacy and compliance. North combines cutting-edge generative and search models with customizable integrations to drive productivity and innovation at scale.




ROLE OVERVIEW

We are seeking an Agent Harness Product Manager to own the execution layer that makes North agents reliable, capable, and production-ready. This is a role that sits at the intersection of three domains:



Agent Loop and Execution. 

Own the core agent runtime: tool orchestration, parallel execution, sub-agent delegation, sandbox code execution, and failure recovery. You will define how North agents plan and act across long, multi-step workflows and ensure the execution environment is robust enough for the most demanding enterprise tasks. You are expected to engage at the implementation level, contributing to architecture decisions alongside engineering rather than simply handing off requirements.



Context Engineering. 

Own how our Agents manage the context window as a deliberately controlled resource. This includes progressive disclosure of tools and skills, context compaction and summarization, offloading of large payloads to a persistent filesystem, and the instrumentation that keeps agents oriented across extended trajectories.



Model-Scaffolding Co-evolution. 

Own the feedback loop between North's harness and the Modeling Team. This PM is the connective tissue that makes that possible: ensuring harness design decisions are validated by Modeling before they are built, that evals are the shared bridge between both teams, and that as the harness evolves the model evolves with it.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Define and own the roadmap for North's agent harness, including the agent loop, context engineering layer, tool orchestration, sandbox execution, and sub-agent delegation

 - Serve as the primary interface between North engineering and Cohere's Modeling team, ensuring new harness capabilities are validated before being built and that neither team paints itself into a corner

 - Own North's agentic evaluation framework, ensuring evals are compatible with both the North harness and Modeling's training infrastructure, and that they serve as a reliable bridge between product and research

 - Engage enterprise customers to surface real-world agentic failures and translate findings into concrete product and model requirements

 - Partner with the agentic expert modeling team to define goals that maximize the impact of our models and prioritize model capabilities and evals most critical for delivering on those goals. Establish a clear roadmap for our agentic modeling capabilities.

 - Stay current with the open-source and commercial agent ecosystem and drive adoption decisions that keep North's architecture aligned with emerging standards.

Who We Are 
 SWTCH is pioneering EV charging solutions for multifamily and commercial properties across North America. Since 2016, our team of entrepreneurs, energy professionals, and technologists has been focused on unlocking the social, economic, and environmental benefits of widespread EV adoption. Today, our solutions are deployed in tens of thousands of locations —many of which are low-to-moderate income housing—helping to make clean mobility accessible for all.
 With an expanding footprint across Canada and the U.S., we’re scaling quickly and looking for mission-driven talent to help accelerate our growth.
 The Role 
 At SWTCH, we're accelerating the adoption of electric vehicles by delivering intelligent charging solutions that make EV charging more accessible, reliable, and efficient. Our platform powers thousands of charging stations across North America, helping property owners, businesses, utilities, and drivers transition to a more sustainable future.
 We're looking for a QA Automation Engineer who is passionate about software quality and automation to help ensure our products are reliable, scalable, and deliver an exceptional customer experience.
 The Opportunity
 Today, our automated test coverage is unit tests and some integration testing — we have no systematic automated coverage of end-to-end user flows. That's the gap this role exists to close. You'll design and build our automated E2E testing practice from the ground up, working closely with Product and Engineering to make sure we stop shipping regressions as we scale. You'll have real latitude here: this isn't a role where testing requirements arrive fully formed. Product can tell you what the product needs to do; figuring out how we verify it actually does that reliably is yours to define.
 How We Work
 Decisions live as close to the work as possible — you'll own how testing gets built, not just execute a checklist someone else wrote.
 We're kind, not nice — we say the hard thing early, in a way that respects the person hearing it. Feedback is specific and timely, not saved for a review cycle.
 We ship in small increments and treat real usage as the fastest way to learn what's working.
 We hold strong opinions loosely — bring conviction, stay open to being wrong.
 What you'll be doing 
 Guide Product Managers in translating use cases into testable requirements and edge cases — PMs bring the "what," you bring the "how do we know it actually works."
 Own the definition of test strategy and testing standards, and design our automated E2E / user-flow testing approach from scratch.
 Develop and execute automated functional, regression, integration, and end-to-end test suites.
 Implement the automated portions of the testing plans you define.
 Mentor and train engineers on writing, maintaining, and extending automated tests — part of this role's mandate is building testing capability across the team, not just within QA.
 Perform manual/exploratory testing where automation isn't yet in place.
 Identify, document, and track defects, working with engineering to drive timely resolution.
 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines.
 Monitor test execution, analyze failures, and continuously improve coverage and reliability.
 What You'll Bring
 5+ years of experience in Software Quality Assurance, including 3+ years focused on test automation.
 Experience in testing web applications, APIs, mobile apps and backend services.
 Experience designing an automated testing practice from scratch — not just extending one that already exists.
 Comfort partnering with Product Managers who rely on you to help surface testing needs and edge cases
 Hands-on experience with test automation frameworks (Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or similar).
 Experience testing REST APIs (Postman or similar).
 Proficiency in Python and/or TypeScript; Ruby experience is a plus given our Rails services.
 Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and Agile practices.
 Experience mentoring or upskilling other engineers in testing practices.
 Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills; excellent communication.
 Nice to Have
 Experience with IoT, connected devices, or hardware-interfacing software — this is the environment you'd be working in day to day, though not a requirement.
 Experience with EV charging, OCPP, or similar device-communication protocols.
 Familiarity with AWS, Azure, or GCP.
 Performance or load testing experience.
 A Note on Our Stack
 We're primarily Python and TypeScript, with React on the frontend and some Ruby on Rails services. We're directionally leaning toward Playwright as our automation framework, but that's not locked in — it's unproven at our scale, and if you've got a strong point of view otherwise, we want to hear it.
 Why Join SWTCH?
 You'll be building something that doesn't exist yet at a company where your judgment on how to build it is genuinely trusted, not just tolerated. If you want ownership over a testing practice from day one — and the chance to shape how an engineering team thinks about quality — we'd love to talk.
